title: ci: Document with a patched roxygen2 that keeps the sentence gap
description:
Split out of #91 so it can be decided on its own.

## The problem

commonmark discards the whitespace a line break stands for. roxygen2 turns every softbreak into a bare newline, so the `.Rd` carries a line break with nothing after it and `Rd2txt()` renders it as a single space. Prose written one sentence per line therefore comes out single-spaced, while the same words wrapped to a fixed width with two spaces after the period keep the gap.

That makes the two styles mutually exclusive: splitting a sentence pair separated by two spaces silently drops one of them. Across the fleet that forced single roxygen lines of 300, 460 and 600 columns, because joining was the only way to keep the gap.

Only the text renderer is affected. `Rd2HTML()` and `Rd2latex()` differ by whitespace that HTML and TeX collapse — and LaTeX applies its own sentence spacing regardless. But text is what `?topic` shows, so it is the version most people read.

## The change

A new composite action, `.github/workflows/roxygen2-fork`, installs roxygen2 from upstream with the `R/` part of `krlmlr/roxygen2@f-sentence-spacing` applied on top, and `R-CMD-check.yaml` runs it immediately before the Roxygenize step.

It shallow-clones upstream, fetches the branch, computes the diff against their merge base restricted to `R/`, and applies it with `git apply --3way`. Restricting to `R/` means an unrelated upstream change to a test fixture cannot fail the documentation step. It aborts if the patch is empty or does not apply, rather than silently installing an unpatched build, and afterwards asserts that what it installed really carries the patch.

`Config/roxygen2/version` becomes `8.1.0.9100`. The `.9100` suffix distinguishes a patched build from upstream's own `.9000` development builds; if upstream moves, the `x.y.z` part follows it and the suffix stays. `DESCRIPTION` is DCF and cannot carry a comment line — `read.dcf()` rejects one as malformed — so the explanation lives in a `Config/cynkra/roxygen2` field.

## Why it is a separate pull request

Taking it changes rendered help across the package; leaving it means the reformatting below it renders exactly as the package renders today, with one space between sentences. Neither half needs the other to be correct, so they should be able to be decided separately.

`man/` is not edited by hand here. CI roxygenises and commits the regenerated `.Rd` files itself, so they arrive on this branch as an automated commit rather than in the hand-written diff, which stays reviewable.

## Upstream

The roxygen2 side is `krlmlr/roxygen2#8`, on the fork, not yet filed with r-lib. It is deliberately narrow: mid-sentence breaks are untouched, links are unaffected, and two guards keep it from firing wrongly — an abbreviation list so a line ending in `e.g.` or `et al.` does not gain a mid-sentence gap, and a fix for a determinism bug where a line starting with `\doi{}` or `\code{}` gained or lost its gap at random, because the test was reading roxygen2's own random placeholder for protected Rd tags.

Part of a fleet-wide pass; the prototype is cynkra/cynkratemplate#131.

title: docs: State the goals and non-goals
description:
Evidence:

- **"bindings are read-only"** — "Binding is read-only." in `R/populate.R`.
- **"does not replace existing names"** — `populate_env()` stops on collisions, also recorded in the 0.1 NEWS entry.
- **"does not reach into C++"** — the README routes that to bindrcpp.
- **"does not grow past the two functions exported since the first release"** — the lifecycle badge says stable, and the exported set has not changed.

The single goal is precise: exactly one addition to `makeActiveBinding()`, namely that the function receives the binding name plus further arguments, with `.envir`/`.enclos` under the caller's control and no dependencies beyond base R.

**One thing I deliberately did not write:** anything calling this package superseded or deprecated. It carries a *stable* lifecycle badge and no statement anywhere says it has been replaced. The maintenance state is expressed only as what the record shows — a fixed API since the first release — rather than as a judgement I am not entitled to make.

Only `README.Rmd`, `README.md` and `index.md` change. Rendered twice, byte-identical.

Stacked on #91, which this PR targets.

title: docs: Break lines at meaning boundaries
description:
Reformatting only, no wording changes. Prose in `README.Rmd` and the roxygen under `R/` now breaks at sentence and clause boundaries rather than wrapping to a fixed width.

The payoff is sentence-level diffs. A reworded sentence touches one line instead of reflowing the paragraph around it, so review sees the change and not the rewrap.

`man/` is not edited by hand here. roxygen2 passes source line breaks straight through to the `.Rd`, and the regenerated files are generated output: CI roxygenises and commits them itself, so they arrive on this branch as an automated commit rather than in the hand-written diff. The rendered help does move, in exactly one way: where a two-space sentence gap was split across lines it narrows to one space. `tools::Rd2txt()` over the topics whose `.Rd` changed puts 1 of 1 in that position — in `create_env.Rd`, `binding.  The function` becomes `binding. The function`. Restoring those gaps is what the patched roxygen2 further up the stack does. `render_readme()` run twice produced byte-identical output, so the rendered README does not move.

`@param fun` in `R/populate.R` keeps a double space between two sentences — `Rd2txt()` renders that literally, so breaking there would change the rendered help. It is re-broken at commas instead, which removes the mid-phrase wrap without touching the gap.

The generation notice at the top of `README.Rmd` was itself wrapped to a fixed width, so two of its sentences started mid-line. It now carries one sentence per line, keeping the five-space continuation indent, matching the form DBI, dm, igraphdata and wrswoR already have. The notice is copied into the rendered files, so `README.md` and `index.md` are re-rendered along with it; the wording is word-for-word unchanged.

One consequence is worth stating plainly. A line break which follows the end of a sentence currently renders as one space, not two, so writing one sentence per line drops the sentence gap from the rendered help. Restoring it needs a patched roxygen2, which is a separate decision: it is #93, stacked on top of this chain, and can be taken or left on its own. Without it this change simply renders as the package renders today.

Part of a fleet-wide pass. r-lib/here#195 is the reference PR, reviewed by hand before the rest were run.

title: docs: Point the coverage badge at the branch that exists
description:
Both halves of the coverage badge referred to `master`, which has not existed since the rename to `main`. The image served that branch's last recorded figure, and the link led to a branch view for a branch that is gone.

The branch is dropped from the image URL rather than corrected. A branch-pinned badge goes stale silently the next time a branch is renamed, which is what happened here; without one, codecov reports the default branch and the badge follows a rename on its own.

The image also moves off the `img.shields.io/codecov/c/` proxy onto codecov's own endpoint, which is what the rest of the fleet uses, and the link onto the `app.` host, which is the UI — the bare `codecov.io` host serves the badge image.

```
image  img.shields.io/codecov/c/github/krlmlr/bindr/master.svg  ->  codecov.io/gh/krlmlr/bindr/graph/badge.svg
link   app.codecov.io/github/krlmlr/bindr?branch=master         ->  app.codecov.io/gh/krlmlr/bindr/tree/main
```

The coverage and CRAN badges also shared a source line, so they rendered side by side while every other badge sits on its own line. Split.

This is part of a fleet-wide badge harmonization; the same correction lands in every repository whose badge drifted.

Stacked on the pkgdown harmonization, which this PR targets, so the diff is the badge change alone.

title: docs: Harmonize README and pkgdown front page rendering
description:
Part of a fleet-wide pkgdown harmonization. Stacked on #86 (the `pak::pak()` README change), which this PR targets, so any conflict surfaces here rather than at merge time. The output format lands in cynkra/cynkratemplate#116, and the CI step that will keep these files current in cynkra/cynkratemplate#118.

## What changes

`README.Rmd` declares `output: cynkratemplate::readme_document` — a `github_document` that also writes the pkgdown front page from the same render, with `-smart` and `--wrap=preserve` so diffs stay sentence-level. Stating the format by name rather than repeating its settings means the settings live in one place instead of thirty.

The `clean_output` hook loses the part that wrote `index.md` and stripped ANSI colour. That is the substantive fix: as a knitr **`document` hook** it ran *before* pandoc, so `index.md` was the pre-pandoc text while `README.md` was the post-pandoc one, and the two then differed by reflowing and smart quotes on top of anything real. The split now happens after pandoc, from one render.

`index.md` is still written here: this README emits ANSI colour, which pkgdown turns into HTML and GitHub shows raw, so the two files genuinely differ.

## Reproducing

```r
rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd")   # or devtools::build_readme(), or Knit
```

Two consecutive renders are byte-identical — checked before committing, because cynkra/cynkratemplate#118 re-renders in CI and commits the result.

title: docs: Use `pak::pak()` for the development install
description:
One of the items `usethis::use_tidy_upkeep_issue()` prescribes for 2023, applied across the package fleet as a single-concern change per repository.

`pak::pak()` resolves system requirements and installs binaries where they exist, so it does not need a compiler for pure-R dependencies the way `install_github()` does.

The `# install.packages("pak")` comment is kept, matching the packages in this fleet that already use pak. pak is not a dependency of usethis, and only devtools imports it (`pak (>= 0.9.5)`), so a reader with neither installed still needs that line.

Both `README.Rmd` and the generated `README.md` are updated in step. The snippet sits in a non-evaluated code block in both, so the edit is textually identical and no rebuild was needed.

Part of a fleet-wide upkeep pass.

title: chore: Migrate from defunct `with_mock()` to `with_mocked_bindings()`
description:
`with_mock()` was deprecated in testthat 3.2.0 and is now defunct. The underlying API functions are being removed in R 4.5.0.

## Changes

- **tests/testthat/test-error.R**: Migrated to `with_mocked_bindings()`
  ```r
  # Before
  with_mock(
    `bindr::to_symbol_encoding` = function(x) paste0(x, "-garbled"),
    expect_warning(...)
  )
  
  # After
  with_mocked_bindings(
    to_symbol_encoding = function(x) paste0(x, "-garbled"),
    .package = "bindr",
    expect_warning(...)
  )
  ```

- **.gitignore**: Added `*.tar.gz` and `*.Rcheck` patterns
